rationale: Blowfish is a small, extremely hot cipher kernel ( BlowfishEncipher/BlowfishDecipher with 16 data-dependent S-box lookups per round, plus a 521-iteration key schedule), with few functions and no function pointers, so the table leans toward cheap, high-yield transformations: SUB gets the strongest weights since arithmetic substitution obscures the round function's XOR/add structure with negligible overhead; FLA and BCF get solid but bounded weights to scramble control flow of the Feistel rounds while keeping RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights low so the driver avoids piling bogus edges into the innermost loops; IGV is moderately favored because the P-array and S-boxes are globals and hiding their layout/identity raises reverse-engineering cost, but its weight is tempered by the per-lookup indirection cost; SPLIT and IBR add diversity at low cost; ICALL is nearly disabled since the program is straight-line C with no indirect-call sites to exploit, and inflating it would only add call overhead in the hot loop. Low CorrectnessRisk weights across the board reflect that this is small, well-defined C where aggressive selection is safe, while the low cost weights keep total overhead acceptable given how runtime-dominated this workload is.
